summary: Oregon Dept. of Forestry cabin on Triangulation Point, Tillamook State Forest: built 1955, emergency-only from 1964, gone by 1966; summit now gated.

facts.design: Wooden live-in cabin built on the ground; register says 12-ft tower, 1955 report says 14x14 cabin
facts.status_note: Used for emergencies only from 1964 and gone by 1966; summit now a gated satellite relay site

staffing.status: emergency use only after 1964; staffed 1957 per local paper

access.note: Summit track passes a gate with a radiofrequency warning sign; South Triangulation Point is an open summit reached by forest roads

visit.trail_note: Open hiking summit is South Triangulation Point, a scramble from the forest roads; do not go past the gate on the summit track

events.note: 1955 annual report to ODF: cabin built on the ground to replace the Cedar Butte lookout; cost of the work excluding furniture was $3,138.63
June 20, 1957 Vernonia Eagle item says Margaret Wells would start work at the lookout the coming Monday
Marked gone 1966 on firelookout.com and in the register caption (1955-1966); Forest Lookouts page says only Removed
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on November 17, 2010

evidence.supports: Cost of the 1955 work excluding furniture: $3,138.63

evidence.quote: 1955 Annual Report to Oregon Department of Forestry

evidence.quote: Built in 1955, this 12' wooden live-in tower was used for emergency only starting in 1964 and is now gone.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register calls the lookout a 12-foot wooden live-in tower; the 1955 report quoted on oregonlookouts.weebly.com describes a 14x14 cabin built on the ground. The story reports both; the cabin-on-the-ground description agrees with the brief's kind ground.

notes_for_editor: Size conflicts between register (12-ft tower) and 1955 report quoted on weebly (14x14 cabin). No source gives a removal date beyond 'gone 1966'; the weebly page says only Removed. Oregon Hikers (undated page, trip reports 2021) describes the gated summit with a satellite relay station; no source describes remains of the cabin. Brief access was unknown; the summit track is gated, so restricted is proposed. Brief kind ground and 2010 registration check out. No photos added.
